title: NAS 410 Audit Documentation in Los Angeles
description: NAS 410 and Nadcap AC7114 audit documents for Los Angeles space, airframe and special-process suppliers, built for your Level 3 to approve. Contact us now.
h1: NAS 410 and Nadcap AC7114 Audit Documentation for Los Angeles Aerospace and Space Suppliers
html:
Southern California's launch companies, spacecraft builders, airframe and defense primes lean on hundreds of smaller shops across the Los Angeles basin for machining, forging, heat treatment and inspection, and every one of those shops with an NDT process answers to NAS 410 and, usually, to a Nadcap AC7114 audit. Atlantis NDT works with Los Angeles suppliers on the audit documentation side: we prepare and check the written practice, records and technique files, and the Responsible Level 3 at your company approves them. Describe your audit and methods and we reply within one business day.

Responsibilities, stated once and plainly

Your company certifies its NDT personnel. Your Responsible Level 3, designated in writing by your management, approves the written practice, the procedures and the examinations. Atlantis is neither of those. We are not your Responsible Level 3, we do not certify personnel to NAS 410, and we do not sell or run NAS 410 training or examinations. Our work is ASNT NDT Level III consulting that makes the approver's job manageable: gap reviews, drafting, record reconstruction, mock audits and help with corrective actions.

That consulting is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, certified by ASNT at Level III for ultrasonic, radiography, magnetic particle, liquid penetrant and visual inspection, with over eleven years of field work across several countries. Technique content in other methods goes to a Level 3 who holds that method. And since Atlantis does not perform radiography in the United States, our involvement with a casting radiography line is limited to Level III review of the RT procedures, technique charts and film or digital image records.

The Los Angeles aerospace map, from Hawthorne to Palmdale

Few regions hold as many kinds of aerospace work inside one county. SpaceX builds and launches rockets from its base in Hawthorne. Northrop Grumman's aerospace systems business is based in Redondo Beach, and the company has expanded its facilities at Air Force Plant 42 in Palmdale as the B-21 bomber program moved forward. Rocket propulsion has a long history in Canoga Park, where the engine maker then known as Aerojet Rocketdyne built propulsion systems including RS-25 engines for NASA. In El Segundo, The Aerospace Corporation supports national security launches as a research organization rather than a hardware maker.

Underneath those names is the part of the industry that faces most NAS 410 audits: the subtier. The basin's industrial corridors, from the South Bay through the Gateway Cities to the San Fernando and Santa Clarita valleys, hold forge shops, foundries, heat treaters, platers, precision machinists and independent NDT houses, many of them family-owned and decades old. A single titanium fitting can pass through four or five of them before it reaches a prime, and several of those stops involve penetrant, magnetic particle or ultrasonic inspection by a different employer each time.

That chain explains why Los Angeles audits feel different. Each shop is audited by Nadcap for its own processes, by the primes it ships to, and by the companies upstream that use it as a subcontractor. The same personnel file can be pulled three times in a quarter by three auditors looking for three different things.

The multi-customer special process house

The typical Los Angeles NDT department serves many customers at once. A penetrant line may run to one prime's specification in the morning and another's after lunch, with different sensitivity levels, different acceptance criteria and different rules on who may evaluate indications. Every one of those differences has to show up somewhere in the written documents, and the technicians have to be certified for what they actually do.

The record that usually fixes this is a customer requirements matrix: one table listing each customer specification and revision, the methods and techniques it calls for, any extra training or examination it demands, any customer approval the shop must hold, and the procedure that implements it. With that matrix, the written practice can stay general while the specific requirements sit in controlled appendices. Without it, the shop ends up with contradictory procedures and a written practice that promises things no one remembers agreeing to. We build the matrix from your purchase orders and specifications, mark each gap, and prepare the appendix text for approval.

A related trap is specification revision drift. Customers update their NDT specifications on their own schedule, and a shop that misses a revision may inspect correctly but cite the wrong document on every report. Our matrix records the revision in force, the date your Level 3 reviewed it, and what changed, so the next auditor sees a controlled process rather than a coincidence.

Customer approval status deserves its own register too. Several primes approve special process sources individually, sometimes in addition to Nadcap, and a shop that ships parts processed by a method for which its approval has lapsed or was never granted has a problem no written practice can fix afterward. A simple register listing each customer, each approved process, the approval reference, its scope and its review date lets the quality manager confirm status at contract review rather than at the audit. We set that register up from your purchase orders and correspondence and link it to the requirements matrix, so the two documents are reviewed together.

Space and launch hardware: tighter technique evidence

Launch vehicles and spacecraft bring requirements that commercial airframe work rarely has at the same intensity. Customers frequently add fracture-control expectations on top of NAS 410 for flight hardware, including evidence that a technique can reliably find flaws of a specified size, part-by-part traceability to serial number, and inspection records kept for the life of the program. Penetrant sensitivity choices, etching before penetrant on machined surfaces where a specification calls for it, and the exact reference standards behind an ultrasonic technique all draw questions.

For these programs we prepare technique files that show the whole chain in one place: the governing specification paragraph, the approved technique sheet, the reference standard and its certification, any capability demonstration your Level 3 conducted, and the certified personnel authorized to run it. We also check that the records procedure states a retention period long enough for the longest-lived program you support. The procedure qualification and demonstration page explains how demonstrations are planned and recorded.

Forgings, castings and heat-treated parts moving through the basin

Much of the region's NDT happens to raw and semi-finished product. Forgings get immersion or contact ultrasonic inspection under specifications such as AMS 2630, castings and machined details get fluorescent penetrant, and steel parts get magnetic particle inspection under ASTM E1444 after heat treatment or grinding. The auditor's questions follow the product: are the reference blocks the right alloy and form, does the scan plan cover the whole volume the specification requires, is each acceptance class tied to the purchase order, and was the inspection done at the stage of manufacture the specification names.

When a part changes hands between shops, documentation gaps appear at the handoff. A forge shop's ultrasonic certification of a billet does not cover a later penetrant inspection at a machinist, and a machinist relying on its supplier's NDT has to show how that supplier was approved and how its reports were reviewed. How a buyer should vet and monitor an NDT supplier is set out on the subcontractor approval audits page.

Personnel record packs that hold up when sampled

An auditor in Los Angeles will often ask for the files of whoever is working on the floor that day, which means every pack has to be complete, not just the few prepared for the visit. A sound pack holds the certification record listing method, level and techniques; training records against an approved course outline with instructor qualification; experience records signed when the work was done; the general, specific and practical examinations with grades and examiner; vision records for near vision and color perception; and the recertification history.

The defects we find most in basin shops are predictable. Experience logs reconstructed from memory months later. Specific examinations that never mention the customer specifications the technician uses. Vision tests done by a clinic with no record of the test method. Certification letters signed by someone other than the person the written practice names. We rebuild the packs against your written practice, list what cannot be reconstructed honestly, and leave the decision on those items to your Responsible Level 3. Our pages on training records and certificates and vision examination records show what each record should contain.

Outside agencies and contract technicians

Southern California has a deep pool of contract NDT technicians, and shops use them to cover peaks. Under NAS 410, a contract technician working in your program still needs your company's certification, issued under your written practice after your Responsible Level 3 has reviewed their training, experience and examinations. A certificate from the staffing company or from a previous employer is evidence, not authorization. The same principle applies to outside agencies that provide training or examinations: they must be named in the written practice, and your Level 3 must control what they do.

We draft the outside-agency clause, prepare an agency qualification checklist, and set up a short onboarding file for contract technicians so their certification under your program is documented before they touch a part. The NAS 410 explainer describes how outside agencies fit into the standard.

The small family shop with a one-person NDT program

Plenty of basin suppliers have one certified Level 2 who also runs receiving inspection, calibration and half the quality paperwork. Those shops rarely employ a Level 3 at all, so their Responsible Level 3 is an outside individual or agency named in the written practice and designated in writing by management. Auditors are comfortable with that arrangement when the evidence shows the outside Level 3 is genuinely in control: approvals dated before use, documented reviews of procedures and examinations, visits or reviews at the frequency the written practice states, and a clear statement of which methods that person holds.

The findings come when the arrangement exists in name only. A designation letter years old, approvals signed in batches the week before an audit, and no record of the outside Level 3 ever seeing the floor all read badly. Atlantis does not take on that designation for anyone. What we do in these shops is prepare the evidence file that shows how your outside Level 3 exercises control, draft the review records in a form that person can sign as the reviews happen, and set up reminders so periodic reviews stop slipping. For a one-person program, that file often decides the outcome of the audit more than any technical document.

Revision 6 in a multi-customer shop

Revision 6 of NAS 410, published in December 2025 through AIA and its distribution partner Accuris, brings a new Appendix D route that lets Level 2 personnel accumulate points toward the initial Level 3 examination, and clarified certification requirements. In a shop with many customers, the harder question is not what the revision says but when each customer will expect it. Some will update their specifications quickly; others will keep citing an earlier revision for a long time. The customer requirements matrix described above is the natural place to track which revision each customer accepts. We prepare a redline of your written practice against Revision 6 and a transition note for your Level 3 to approve, written so it can be shown to auditors.

How the work runs, and what to send

Document review and drafting are done remotely, with export-controlled files handled the way you specify, and site visits in the Los Angeles area cover the mock audit and floor observation. A mock audit follows AC7114 and your slash sheets, samples personnel files from the floor rather than from a prepared stack, and ends with a ranked findings list. After a real audit, we help prepare root-cause analyses and the objective evidence the Nadcap task group or customer auditor expects before closing each finding. Nadcap AC7114 audit readiness describes the audit in detail.

To begin, gather your written practice, the customer specifications and purchase order quality clauses you work to, the current personnel certification roster, and your most recent audit reports. If certification and calibration due dates live in several spreadsheets, our audit evidence scramble guide shows how to bring them into one place.

Other Atlantis pages for the region include NDT consulting in Los Angeles, aerospace NDT in Los Angeles, third-party inspection in Los Angeles and ASME audit support in Los Angeles for shops that also build pressure equipment. The national overview sits at NAS 410 audit compliance documentation, and NAS 410 versus SNT-TC-1A helps when technicians arrive from industrial NDT backgrounds.

faq.q: We serve a dozen primes. Do we need a written practice for each one?
faq.a: Rarely. A single written practice that implements NAS 410, backed by a controlled customer requirements matrix and appendices for each customer's extra demands, is easier to keep current and easier for auditors to follow. Separate documents for each customer tend to contradict each other within a year.

faq.q: Can a contract technician from a staffing agency work under their agency's certification?
faq.a: Not in a NAS 410 program. The technician needs your company's certification, issued after your Responsible Level 3 has reviewed their training, experience and examination evidence under your written practice. The agency's paperwork is input to that decision, not a substitute for it.

faq.q: Does Atlantis certify technicians or act as our Responsible Level 3?
faq.a: No to both. Atlantis is not a Responsible Level 3 for any client, does not certify personnel to NAS 410 and does not run NAS 410 training or examinations. We prepare and review documentation that your own Level 3 approves and your company issues.

faq.q: Our customer updated its penetrant specification. What do we need to show the auditor?
faq.a: Evidence that your Level 3 reviewed the new revision, a record of what changed, updated procedures or technique sheets if the change affects them, any retraining that followed, and reports that cite the current revision from the effective date onward. We help build that trail.

faq.q: Can you help with our casting radiography line?
faq.a: Atlantis does not perform radiography in the United States. We can review RT procedures, technique charts, image quality records and the qualification files of your radiographic personnel as a Level III, and prepare that documentation for your RT Level 3 to approve.

faq.q: What makes space hardware audits harder than commercial airframe audits?
faq.a: Customers often add fracture-control expectations: evidence that techniques reliably find flaws of a set size, serial-number traceability and lifetime record retention. The technique file has to show the specification, approval, reference standard, any demonstration and authorized personnel together.

faq.q: How long should we keep NDT records for launch vehicle work?
faq.a: As long as your contracts require, which for flight hardware can be the life of the program or longer. Your records procedure should name the longest period any customer demands, not a generic number. Check each purchase order's quality clauses.

faq.q: Will you visit our shop in the basin for the mock audit?
faq.a: Yes. Observation of real jobs and random file pulls only work in person, so the mock audit is normally done on site, while document drafting is remote. Staff fly in from the Houston or Hyderabad office to handle the on-site part.

faq.q: Can our technicians use Atlantis courses toward NAS 410?
faq.a: Atlantis courses follow ASNT SNT-TC-1A and are not NAS 410 courses. Whether any outside training hours can be credited in a NAS 410 program is your Responsible Level 3's decision, recorded under your written practice. See NDT training in Los Angeles for what the courses cover.
